walkthroughs.body_html:
Stars — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Stars brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Stars.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

About 6,000 years.
About 13.8 billion years.
Infinite.
Infinite.

Ellipses (Kepler's first law), with the Sun at one focus.

mcqs.q: What is the principle behind stellar parallax?
options: Stars actually move position throughout the year.
Straight lines that bend.
A nearby star appears to shift against background stars as Earth orbits the Sun.
Telescopes distort star positions.
